_note: What Ren, who carries the post, says when the farmer talks to him (Talk, README.md, Villagers): the first pick whose if holds names the lines, one of them by the day; gift_ lines answer a gift by its reaction, gift_items his own answers to a daruma and to dishes. At the counter he talks of the sorting, on Sundays of his day off. The birthday lines (spring 15), the close lines from band 4, the round lines once his band 5 scene is seen (heart_ren_5), the dear lines at band 6 once his band 6 scene is (heart_ren_6) until he is promised; engaged_ lines once he said yes to the knot, and married (married_ren) help_ lines on a morning he did a chore, wed_morning_ / wed_evening_ at the farmhouse and wed_out_ elsewhere (data/marriage.json). He talks a lot and knows who writes to whom, never what. Our own lines.

lines.speaker: ren
lines.text: Blossom Day! Half my bag this week was invitations to it. The other half was people saying they can't come. They all came.

lines.speaker: ren
lines.text: Lanterns everywhere. I know who sent which one to whom. I'm not telling. I'm just smiling.

lines.speaker: ren
lines.text: Moon Night is the one night nobody writes letters. They just look up. Even I take my bag off.

lines.speaker: ren
lines.text: Tomorrow morning the New Year cards come in. Hundreds. My busiest day, and my favorite.

lines.speaker: ren
lines.text: Back again? Careful, I'll start delivering your news too.

lines.speaker: ren
lines.text: Twice in a day. If you've got a letter, I'll take it. If not, walk with me a bit.

lines.speaker: ren
lines.text: You're the new farmer! Ren, the post. I know your name already. It was on three letters before you got here.

lines.speaker: ren
lines.text: Don't worry. I know who writes to whom. I never know what they say. That's the rule.

lines.speaker: ren
lines.text: Rain or shine, the post goes out. My bag's oilcloth. My socks are not.

lines.speaker: ren
lines.text: Sending something? Stamps are on the left. Gossip's free, but I don't give it out.

lines.speaker: ren
lines.text: Sorting the afternoon bag. Sakurazaka writes the most. Kaminoda writes the longest.

lines.speaker: ren
lines.text: Sunday. The post office is shut and my feet are on holiday. I'm reading other people's books today, not their letters.

lines.speaker: ren
lines.text: Snow on the round means I can see my own footprints from yesterday. Same path. Every day. I like that.

lines.speaker: ren
lines.text: Genzo writes to a seed company every month to complain. Then he orders more seed. Every month.

lines.speaker: ren
lines.text: I walk about twelve kilometers a day. Kota asked if I've walked to the moon yet. Not yet. Close.

lines.speaker: ren
lines.text: Tome's letters to the city are the thickest in the valley. I can't say what's in them. I can say they're heavy.

lines.speaker: ren
lines.text: You know it's my birthday? Then I'm off duty. Find me by the pond, reading. Don't bring letters!

lines.speaker: ren
lines.text: For me? Nobody hands me things. I hand things to people. ...This is a strange feeling. A good one.

lines.speaker: ren
lines.text: I walk past your farm twice a day now. It's not on the way. I just like the view.

lines.speaker: ren
lines.text: People tell me things they'd never write down. I keep those too. Yours I keep closest.

lines.speaker: ren
lines.text: Still on foot, still on time. The head office keeps asking how. I tell them: good boots, good people.

lines.speaker: ren
lines.text: I timed the round today. Four minutes slower than last year. Everyone wants to chat now. Your fault.

lines.speaker: ren
lines.text: I wrote you a second letter. Then a third. They're in my bag. I'm working up to it.

lines.speaker: ren
lines.text: Your farm's the first stop now. The whole round starts better that way.

lines.speaker: ren
lines.text: Sayo asked why I whistle on the way to the farm and not on the way back. I said the bag's lighter going. It isn't.

lines.speaker: ren
lines.text: Three days! I've told nobody. Well. Everyone. They told me first.

lines.speaker: ren
lines.text: I keep checking my own name on the shrine notice. It's real. I delivered it myself.

lines.speaker: ren
lines.text: Morning! I'm off on the round. Anything to post? Love letters are half price for family.

lines.speaker: ren
lines.text: Tea's on. I've had mine. The bag waits for no one, not even you.

lines.speaker: ren
lines.text: Your farm is still the first stop. I just walk out of the front door now. Shortest round in history.

lines.speaker: ren
lines.text: Home! Twelve kilometers and every house in the valley. This one's my favorite.

lines.speaker: ren
lines.text: Sit down, I'll tell you the day's news. The parts I'm allowed to, anyway.

lines.speaker: ren
lines.text: My feet are tired. My mouth isn't. Shall I tell you about the goat in Kaminoda?

lines.speaker: ren
lines.text: I watered the dry plots before the round. Plants are easier than people. They don't ask for news.

lines.speaker: ren
lines.text: The rows by the path looked thirsty, so I gave them a can. Delivered.

lines.speaker: ren
lines.text: I filled the coop's feed box. The hens are my easiest customers. Never a complaint.

lines.speaker: ren
lines.text: The feed's in the coop, from your sack. Signed for by one very loud hen.

lines.speaker: ren
lines.text: Married, and still the post. People hand me letters for you now. I say: I'll see them tonight.

lines.speaker: ren
lines.text: Tome says I talk less since the wedding. I don't. I just talk about you more.

lines.speaker: ren
lines.text: For me? Oh, this is exactly right. You've been reading my mind, not my mail.

lines.speaker: ren
lines.text: That's kind of you. Thanks! It'll ride in the bag with me.

lines.speaker: ren
lines.text: Oh, thanks. Delivered, and received.

lines.speaker: ren
lines.text: Ah. That's not really for me. Thanks for thinking of me, though.

lines.speaker: ren
lines.text: A stone? I've got enough weight in my bag, thank you.

lines.speaker: ren
lines.text: Another? One a day, like the post. Save it for tomorrow.

lines.speaker: ren
lines.text: A daruma! One eye now, and the other when the round's walked a thousand times. I'll put it on my chest.

lines.speaker: ren
lines.text: You cooked this? Lunch on the round, with something from home. Thank you!

lines.speaker: ren
lines.text: Still warm! I'll eat it at the counter.

lines.speaker: ren
lines.text: A dish! Thanks, that's supper.

lines.speaker: ren
lines.text: Ah, that's a bit fancy for me. I eat walking. Sorry.
